title: Something Warm at the Door: How a Pet Quietly Fills a Lonely Day
title_zh: 门边的温暖：宠物如何悄悄填满孤独的一天
intro_zh: 本文约536词，围绕宠物给独居青年与老人带来的陪伴展开，含具体研究数据与真实生活场景，共标注6个CET-4核心词，难度适中，理解目标约85%-90%。

paragraphs.en: At six o'clock on a winter evening, the sound of a key turning in the lock wakes a small animal on the other side of the door. Before the owner can put down her bag, a dog is jumping up or a cat is rubbing against her legs. For many people who live alone, this may be the warmest minute of the day.
paragraphs.zh: 冬日傍晚六点，钥匙在锁孔里一转，门那边的一只小动物就醒了。主人还没来得及放下包，狗已经跳起来，或者猫已经开始蹭她的腿。对许多独居的人来说，这也许是整天里最温暖的一分钟。

paragraphs.en: In China, single-person households have grown fast in the past ten years. Many young workers move to big cities where parents and old friends are hundreds of kilometers away. A pet cannot pay the rent or answer a difficult email, yet it fills the silent space in a small flat. When owners are asked why they keep an animal, most give the same answer: companionship.
paragraphs.zh: 在中国，单人家庭在过去十年里增长得很快。许多年轻打工者搬到大城市，父母和老朋友都在几百公里之外。宠物付不了房租，也回不了一封难回的邮件，但它填满了小公寓里安静的空间。当主人被问到为什么养动物时，大多数人给出同样的答案：陪伴。

paragraphs.en: Scientists say this feeling is more than imagination. In one experiment, volunteers spent just fifteen minutes touching a friendly dog. Afterwards, the level of cortisol, a hormone connected with stress, fell in their blood. Their heart rate also slowed slightly. The dogs understood nothing about the test; they simply sat close and stayed quiet. The human body, however, reacted as if a heavy coat had been taken off.
paragraphs.zh: 科学家说，这种感觉不只是想象。在一项实验里，志愿者只花了十五分钟抚摸一只友善的狗。之后，他们血液中与压力有关的一种激素——皮质醇的水平下降了。他们的心率也略微减缓。狗对这项测试一无所知；它们只是靠得很近，安安静静地待着。然而人的身体却仿佛脱掉了一件沉重的外套。

paragraphs.en: A pet also gives shape to the day. A dog must be walked, fed and brushed at about the same time every morning and night. This ordinary routine may sound boring, but it is surprisingly powerful. Owners often say they get out of bed on days when they would rather hide under the blanket. The dog does not care about moods or deadlines. It only wants breakfast, and it wants it now.
paragraphs.zh: 宠物也给一天赋予形状。狗必须在每天早晚差不多的时间被遛、被喂、被梳毛。这套普通的日常安排听起来可能无聊，却出人意料地有力量。主人常说，在那些他们宁愿躲在被子里的日子里，他们还是起了床。狗不在乎情绪，也不在乎截止日期。它只想要早饭，而且现在就要。

paragraphs.en: There is a social side as well. Dog owners stop and chat in parks even when they have never met before. A study in Britain found that pet owners were more likely to know their neighbors by name. The animal works as a bridge between strangers. It gives them a safe, easy topic, and a conversation that no one has planned can last for twenty minutes.
paragraphs.zh: 还有社交的一面。遛狗的人在公园里即使从未见过面，也会停下来聊上几句。英国的一项研究发现，养宠物的人更可能叫得出邻居的名字。动物成了陌生人之间的桥梁。它给了他们一个安全、轻松的话题，一场没人计划过的对话能持续二十分钟。

paragraphs.en: For older people the effect can be stronger. Grandparents whose children live in faraway cities often describe a cat or a small dog as a member of the family. A seventy-eight-year-old woman in Shanghai said her dog gave her a reason to leave her flat three times a day. Without him, she admitted, she might not speak to another person until the evening news began.
paragraphs.zh: 对老年人来说，这种作用可能更强。子女住在远方城市的祖辈，常常把一只猫或一只小狗说成家庭成员。上海一位七十八岁的女士说，她的狗给了她一天出门三次的理由。她承认，要是没有它，她可能直到晚间新闻开始都不会和另一个人说上一句话。

paragraphs.en: Of course, a pet is not a simple answer to loneliness. Food, medical care and daily time all cost something. A cat may live fifteen years; a large dog, ten or more. Anyone who brings an animal home accepts a real responsibility. It cannot be returned to the shop like a borrowed book, and it should not be chosen in a single excited afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 当然，宠物并不是解决孤独的简单答案。食物、医疗和每天的时间都要付出代价。一只猫可能活十五年；一只大狗，十年甚至更久。任何把动物带回家的人，都承担着一份真正的责任。它不能像一本借来的书那样被退回店里，也不该在某个一时兴起的下午被草率选中。

paragraphs.en: Yet for many owners the trade is clearly worth it. A pet offers something a phone screen never can: a living creature that waits at the door, listens without judging, and reminds its owner that someone depends on them. The loyal little figure sleeping on the sofa may not solve any problem, but it makes the evening feel less empty. In a busy world, that kind of comfort is not small at all.
paragraphs.zh: 然而对很多主人来说，这笔交换显然是值得的。宠物提供的东西，是手机屏幕永远给不了的：一个活着的生命，在门口等你，不带评判地听你说话，并提醒主人，有人依赖着他们。沙发上那团忠心的小身影也许解决不了任何问题，但它让傍晚不那么空落。在忙碌的世界里，这份安慰并不小。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to train a dog with scientific methods.
How pets bring companionship and daily structure to people who feel alone.
Why the cost of keeping pets keeps rising in big cities.
How animals help scientists study human hormones.
questions.explain: 全文从独居者回家被迎接的场景出发，谈到陪伴、减压研究、日常规律、社交桥梁、老年人案例以及养宠的责任，主线是宠物给孤独的人带来陪伴与生活结构，故选B。A、C、D都只涉及文中某个细节或完全未提。

questions.q: According to paragraph 3, what happened to volunteers after fifteen minutes with a dog?
options: The level of a stress-related hormone in their blood dropped.
The dogs became cleverer than before.
questions.explain: 第三段明确说，与狗相处十五分钟后，志愿者血液中与压力有关的激素（皮质醇）水平下降，心率也略微减缓，故选B。文中并未提记忆力提升（A），也没有说狗变聪明（C），血压是下降而非上升（D）。

questions.q: Why does the author mention the seventy-eight-year-old woman in Shanghai?
options: To prove that pets are only suitable for the elderly.
To give an example of how a pet gives an older person a reason to go out and company.
To show that cats are easier to keep than dogs.
To explain why keeping pets is expensive in Chinese cities.
questions.explain: 该例子紧接“对老年人的作用可能更强”，说明狗让她一天出门三次，否则可能一整天无人交谈，属于典型的举例论证，故选B。文中并未说宠物只适合老人（A），也未比较猫狗（C），此例不涉及花费（D）。

questions.q: What does the underlined phrase 'the trade' in paragraph 7 most probably mean?
options: A business deal in a pet shop.
Giving money, time and care in exchange for a pet's company.
A bargain between pet hospitals and pet owners.
questions.explain: 第七段先讲养宠要付出食物、医疗和时间等代价，随后说“对很多主人来说这笔交换显然是值得的”，因此the trade指用金钱、时间和精力换取宠物的陪伴，故选B。其余选项都把它误解为具体买卖或交易行为。
